summary: Every top 10 film is a household name, but sequels and recent hits beat the classics: Up is #11, Monsters, Inc. #16, the first Toy Story #21. Toy Story 5 at #3 keeps it current.
reasons: Casual found 6 (Finding Nemo, Incredibles 2, Inside Out 2, Toy Story 3, Coco, Finding Dory) and lost lives on the classics: the first Toy Story (picked from the free 'toy story' menu), Up, Monsters, Inc., Cars and Ratatouille. Tapping a sequel from that menu instead finds 7. Every miss shows its gross, and 'sequels win' is a lesson players learn mid-game.

Sequels typed every way work ('toy story four', 'inside out two', 'the incredibles 2', 'finding nemo 2', 'monsters u'); 'toy story', 'finding' and 'inside' offer the films; 'pixar', 'disney' and other studios' films (Frozen, Shrek, Zootopia 2, Moana, Minions) are free.
The fan swept 10/10 without a miss; a casual Blitz names about 21 Pixar titles in 90 seconds and scores 20 (Frozen is free).
fixes: Finding Nemo (#7) shows $871,014,978, its 2003 run only, as the List of Pixar films box office table gives it, while that table's Toy Story and Toy Story 2 figures include re-releases. Its own article gives $940.3 million with the 2012 3D re-release. Monsters, Inc. ($528,773,250, $255.9 million domestic) also leaves out its 2012 re-release; its lifetime gross (about $577 million, check its article) would move it from #16 above Cars 2 and Brave. Top 10 and its order are unchanged: override these two values with lifetime grosses in scripts/topics.ts (pixar-films) at the next rebuild.
